what_it_does: When many GPUs train an AI model together, they must periodically sum up each GPU's local gradient updates (the corrections computed each training step) into one shared result and distribute it back to everyone — a collective operation called AllReduce. Existing AllReduce algorithms were designed for abstract network topologies and then adapted to the physical 2D grid (mesh) networks that connect real GPU clusters; this mismatch wastes some of the available network bandwidth. TidalMesh designs an AllReduce algorithm from scratch for a 2D mesh, routing data in wave-like sweeps that move naturally along the grid rows and columns, using both directions of every link simultaneously, so no link sits idle while others are saturated. A further optimization called "collective communication unrolling" overlaps different phases of the AllReduce with each other across consecutive training iterations, hiding the communication time behind ongoing computation.
